title: LLMs As MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
authors: H. Je-Gal, J. Kim, C. Yi, and H.-S. Lee
venue: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026
lead: A robot simulator can run without errors even when its reward teaches the wrong behavior.
body: ARPG takes a written task and builds the reinforcement learning problem in stages. Its agents record the objective and constraints before defining what the robot observes, which actions it can take, and how it earns reward. A checker traces inconsistencies back to the relevant stage. Separate agents then implement the simulator and train a policy in Isaac Lab.
takeaway: In 10 independent attempts per task, ARPG produced a successful policy 9 times for Ant and 9 for Franka Reach. For Franka Lift, the simulator ran in 9 attempts and only 4 yielded a successful lifting policy.
caption: ARPG framework · Figure 2 in the manuscript.
alt: ARPG pipeline from task and robot descriptions through sequential MDP modeling, validation, simulator implementation and policy training.

title: Factorized Scheduling Principle: Learning Interpretable and Transferable Policies via Structured Additive Functions
lead: Which item should a scheduler serve next when the number of candidates keeps changing?
body: FSP learns one priority rule from scheduling experience. It represents the current candidates by the distribution of their features and scores each item by adding learned effects for individual features and pairs of features. The resulting curves show what raised or lowered an item's priority. The same rule can rank a different number of candidates without retraining.
takeaway: The authors tested wireless scheduling, inventory replenishment, and warehouse clearance. In warehouse clearance, a rule trained on 10 items earned the highest average reward among the tested methods on new populations of 5, 10, 15, and 20 items.
caption: FSP framework · Figure 1 in the paper.
alt: FSP overview: candidate items, condition distribution, additive global scheduling principle, and priority scoring and selection.

title: A-LAMP: Agentic LLM-Based Framework for Automated MDP Modeling and Policy Generation
authors: Hong Je-Gal, Chan-Bin Yi, and Hyun-Suk Lee
venue: NeurIPS Workshop on Multi-Turn Interactions in Large Language Models, 2025
lead: Can a written task specification become a working learning environment and a trained policy?
body: A-LAMP divides the work among language-model agents. They identify the quantities, constraints, and objective in the description, then define the state, actions, and rewards. Coding agents turn that formulation into a Gym-style environment and training loop. A code executor runs it and returns errors for repair. The evaluation scores the formulation, executable code, and learned behavior separately.
takeaway: In 20 drone-delivery trials, A-LAMP with GPT-4o produced a successful policy 9 times, compared with 2 for GPT-4o alone. In wireless resource allocation the corresponding counts were 9 and 4.
caption: Human and A-LAMP workflows · Figure 1 in the paper.
alt: Comparison of a human expert workflow with A-LAMP agents for abstract task interpretation, MDP formulation, and coding.

title: Time-Series Explanatory Fault Prediction Framework for Marine Main Engine Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
authors: H. Je-Gal, Y.-S. Park, S.-H. Park, J.-U. Kim, J.-H. Yang, S. Kim, and H.-S. Lee
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering, 12(8), 1296, 2024
lead: When a model predicts an engine fault, which sensor readings prompted the warning, and when did they occur?
body: Using operating data from an LNG carrier, the authors select relevant sensor channels with correlation and SHAP analysis. An LSTM forecasts cylinder exhaust-gas temperature. A learned mask then highlights the sensors and time intervals that influenced the forecast. To check those explanations against known precursors, the authors add 11 synthetic fault patterns to normal operating data.
takeaway: Across the 11 datasets, the mean overlap score was 0.76. It measures the fraction of the time flagged as important for a sensor that fell within its injected precursor period.
caption: Training and explanation framework · Author’s research presentation.
alt: Marine engine prediction framework with correlation and SHAP based feature selection, model training and time-specific explanations.

title: A Novel Data-Driven Soft Sensor in Metaverse Provisioning Predictive Credibility Based on Uncertainty Quantification
authors: S.-H. Park, H. Je-Gal, and H.-S. Lee
lead: A virtual air-quality sensor estimates ultrafine dust from other air-quality and weather measurements. How can it signal that a reading is uncertain?
body: The researchers trained five neural networks on atmospheric measurements from Seoul. Each network estimates both a mean and a variance. Together they produce a dust estimate and an interval around it. The experiment introduced an artificial shift in sensor data, either only at test time or during both training and testing.
takeaway: When the shift first appeared at test time, the intervals were about 12 times wider on average than when training had included the shift. Those wider intervals contained 95.64% of the measured test values.
caption: Soft-sensing system and predictive credibility · Figure 1 in the paper.
alt: Multiple physical sensors provide measurements to a soft sensor, which estimates a target sensor value and its predictive credibility.

short: Time–Frequency Fusion for Marine Engine Fault Detection
title: A Novel Time–Frequency Feature Fusion Approach for Robust Fault Detection in a Marine Main Engine
authors: H. Je-Gal, S.-J. Lee, J.-H. Yoon, H.-S. Lee, J.-H. Yang, and S. Kim
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering, 11(8), 1577, 2023
lead: Can a single shaft encoder reveal a cylinder misfire when engine speed is sampled less frequently?
body: During a sea trial on a crude oil carrier, the researchers deliberately induced a cylinder misfire and recorded instantaneous engine speed. They combined time-domain features of the speed signal with features from its bispectrum, which captures relationships between frequency components. They then reduced the sampling rate to test which fault signatures survived.
takeaway: At one hundredth of the original sampling rate, the fused features classified normal and abnormal operation with 96.26% accuracy. Using the time-domain features alone gave 53.48% on the same test.
caption: Feature-fusion framework · Figure 6 in the paper (CC BY 4.0).
alt: RPM data split into time-domain and frequency-domain feature extraction, then combined for neural-network fault detection.

title: Efficient Federated Digital Twin Synchronization in Edge-Cloud Collaborative System
authors: J.-W. Kim, H. Je-Gal, and H.-S. Lee
lead: Where should each digital twin hand its computation from an edge device to the cloud?
body: A twin can finish inference at an early exit or send an intermediate result to the cloud. The best handoff depends on how often each exit is used, how long each layer takes, and how much data must cross the link. The authors compare a joint search over all twins' split points with a cheaper heuristic that chooses a split for each twin separately.
takeaway: In simulations using an early-exit ResNet on CIFAR-10, the heuristic came close to the exhaustive search's synchronization time. When transmission became costly, sending all inputs to the cloud was the slowest option tested.
caption: Edge–cloud collaboration and early exits · Figure 1 in the paper.
alt: Digital twin networks split neural inference between edge and cloud, with multiple early-exit points.

title: Digital Role-Model Twin Using Reinforcement Learning Model
authors: J.-W. Kim, H. Je-Gal, S.-J. Lee, and H.-S. Lee
venue: The Journal of Korean Institute of Communications and Information Sciences, 48(2), 282–293, 2023
lead: Can a recommender learn how one person's choices change with the situation?
body: The digital role-model twin learns from the choices a role model makes among a set of options. A deep Q-network uses a learned representation of that role model together with contextual information to score the options. In a simulated news service, virtual role models had different interests and became more interested in weather news when it rained or snowed.
takeaway: In rain or snow, the context-aware twin scored 99.18% on the paper's modified recall measure for news recommendations. The version that omitted context scored 90.31% in the same simulation.
caption: Digital role-model twin structure · Figure 1 in the paper.
alt: Role models and contextual decision features feed a shared preference network that offers role-model-specific preferences to users.
